settings.heading: We made coffee for the places we'd rather be.
settings.body: That's not a slogan, it's the whole reason this exists. Here's the short version of why — and where the coffee actually comes from.

This started the way most good ideas do — annoyed by something small. A trip with no signal, a coffee setup built for a kitchen instead of a backpack, and a compostable filter that somehow made the best cup of the week. That felt worth building around.

Offline was never about avoiding technology. It's just coffee that doesn't need any — steeped in a tent, a kitchen, or a hotel room with nothing but a kettle. Hot water and five minutes were always the whole recipe. Everything else was optional.
settings.sign_off: — Not signed. That's kind of the point.

settings.text: We buy direct from a handful of farms we visit each year. Smaller lots, fairer prices, and a list of names instead of a co-op number.
The coffee gets roasted in small batches in Brooklyn, ground the same week, and sealed into a compostable filter. Then it leaves the warehouse and shows up at your door.

settings.quote: "You can drink coffee with two bars of signal, or no bars at all. The coffee doesn't care. Maybe you don't either."
